content_html:
Traveling to Cusco with children can be an unforgettable experience if planned in advance. The city offers history, culture and impressive landscapes, but also challenges such as altitude and long walks. With good organization, your family will be able to enjoy a comfortable and safe trip.

1. Pre-trip planning

When to travel?

The best time to visit Cusco with children is during the dry season (May to September), since there is less rain and the roads are more accessible.

How to prepare for altitude

Cusco is located 3,399 meters above sea level, so it is important to prevent altitude sickness:
Arrive in Cusco a day in advance to acclimatize before taking excursions.
Rest the first day and avoid strenuous activities.
Drink coca tea or coca candies (for children over 5 years old).
Stay hydrated and eat light.

2. Where to stay with children

Search hotels comfortable, central and with family facilities, such as spacious rooms and breakfast included. Some recommended options are:
Tierra Viva Cusco Center – Comfortable and with an excellent location.
Novotel Cusco – It has an interior patio ideal for children.
Casa Andina Premium Cusco – High quality service and calm environment.

If you travel with babies, make sure the hotel has cribs, hot water and heating.

3. Food for children in Cusco

Peruvian cuisine is varied, but some dishes can be very spicy for children. Some safe options are:
Quinoa soup – Light and nutritious.
grilled chicken – A classic that everyone likes.
Lomo saltado – Meat with fries and rice.

Local markets, such as Saint Peter, they have natural juices and fresh fruits. In addition, there are restaurants with children's menus such as La Bodega 138 (homemade pizzas) or Cicciolina (varied food with options for children).

4. Activities and tours recommended for families

Cusco has many options to enjoy with children without them getting too tired:

Historic Center (1st day – acclimatization)

Visit the Plaza de Armas and its surroundings.
Explore the Inka Museum, which has interactive exhibits.
Walk through the neighborhood Saint Blaise, where there are artisan workshops.

Sacred Valley of the Incas (2nd day – lower altitude)

The Sacred Valley is at a lower altitude than Cusco and is perfect for a day of exploration:
Awanakancha – A center where children can feed llamas and alpacas.
Pisac – Craft market with colorful souvenirs.
Moray and Maras – Circular agricultural terraces and salt mines, very visual for children!

Machu Picchu with children (3rd or 4th day)

The ideal is to take the train from Ollantaytambo to avoid long walks.
Bring a light backpack with snacks, water and sunscreen.
Use a baby carrier instead of a stroller, as the path is uneven.
Explain the history of Machu Picchu in a fun way with stories about the Incas.

Other family activities

  • Saqsayhuamán Park – An archaeological site with large spaces to run and play.
  • Cochahuasi Rescue Center – An animal shelter with condors and pumas.
  • Cusco Planetarium – To learn about the stars from an Andean perspective.
